'''Birol Emir''' (born 1966) is a [[Turkish Americans|Turkish-American]] [[statistician]]. He is an Executive Director and head of Real-World Evidence Statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Birol EMIR {{!}} Director, & Adjunct Professor {{!}} Ph.D. {{!}} Statistics {{!}} Research profile |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Birol-Emir |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810160257/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Birol-Emir |archive-date=2023-08-10 |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=ResearchGate |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> at [[Pfizer|Pfizer Inc.]]. He has been serving as an adjunct professor of statistics<ref>{{Cite web |title=Birol Emir {{!}} Columbia University School of Professional Studies |url=https://sps.columbia.edu/person/birol-emir |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=sps.columbia.edu |language=en}}</ref> and lecturer of Applied Analytics at [[Columbia University]] in New York City. Additionally, he serves as an external committee member of the Graduate School of Arts and Science for the Ph.D. degree at [[Rutgers University]].

== Education ==
Birol grew up in [[Turkey|Turkiye]] and graduated from [[Middle East Technical University]] with a B.S. with Honors. He earned his M.S. and Ph.D. in statistics from [[Iowa State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Iowa State Alumnus Dr. Birol Emir Named ASA Fellow |url=https://www.stat.iastate.edu/news/2025/iowa-state-alumnus-dr-birol-emir-named-asa-fellow |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Department of Statistics |language=en}}</ref> He completed post-doctoral work for the National Surgical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project at the [[University of Pittsburgh Medical Center]].

== Research and Career ==
Birol's areas of research and professional expertise lie in [[causal inference]], [[Real world evidence|real-world evidence]] generation, [[Predictive modelling|predictive modeling]], [[big data]], and [[clinical trial]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Birol Emir |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=KshUxh0AAAAJ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> He co-authored the book ''Interface Between Regulation and Statistics in Drug Development'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Interface between Regulation and Statistics in Drug Development |url=https://www.routledge.com/Interface-between-Regulation-and-Statistics-in-Drug-Development/Alemayehu-Emir-Gaffney/p/book/9780367608286 |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}</ref> co-edited the book ''Statistical Topics in Healthcare Economics and Outcomes Research'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistical Topics in Health Economics and Outcomes Research |url=https://www.routledge.com/Statistical-Topics-in-Health-Economics-and-Outcomes-Research/Alemayehu-Cappelleri-Emir-Zou/p/book/9781032096049 |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}</ref> and authored a chapter in ''A Picture is Worth a Thousand Tables: Graphics in Life Sciences''<ref>{{cite book |date=2012 |editor-last=Krause |editor-first=Andreas |editor2-last=O'Connell |editor2-first=Michael |title=A Picture is Worth a Thousand Tables |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4614-5329-1  |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4614-5329-1 |isbn=978-1-4614-5328-4 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Awards and honors ===
Birol was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA) in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Applied Analytics Lecturer Selected as a Fellow in the American Statistical Association {{!}} Columbia University School of Professional Studies |url=https://sps.columbia.edu/news/applied-analytics-lecturer-selected-fellow-american-statistical-association |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=sps.columbia.edu |language=en}}</ref>
